nodes.label: Cross-platform build matrix
nodes.rationale: macOS/Linux/Windows build in parallel with fail-fast disabled so one platform's packaging failure still yields the other two artefacts for inspection.

nodes.label: Frozen uv dependency install
nodes.rationale: uv sync --frozen with a pinned Python 3.13 makes the release build resolve exactly the locked dependency set — the binary is built from uv.lock, never from a fresh resolution.

nodes.label: GitHub release publication job
nodes.rationale: A separate job gated on the build matrix collects every platform zip and publishes one GitHub release, so a partial matrix never produces a half-populated release.

nodes.label: PyInstaller standalone bundle
nodes.rationale: SupraSimFit.spec drives a self-contained bundle per OS so end users never install Python; the per-OS packaging steps normalise the output to a single zip naming scheme.

nodes.label: Pint contexts deliberately unused
nodes.rationale: Every conversion here is a same-dimension scale change (uM to M), so plain .to() suffices; a context would only be warranted for a genuine cross-dimension conversion such as Ka to delta-G.

nodes.label: Deliberate non-changes
nodes.rationale: Column-name unit auto-detection was excluded because a heuristic classifier could itself produce the silent wrong conversions the design removes; condition exception types stayed as pint.DimensionalityError rather than being churned; the reciprocal display generalisation was skipped to avoid regressing the working 1/M -> M^-1 path.

nodes.label: Multi-agent re-audit after merging main
nodes.rationale: The branch was rebased onto main and a full multi-agent re-audit re-ran on the merged tree, which is what exposed the half-wired self-describing-unit work — the merge-conflict surface and the re-audit surface were the same files.

nodes.label: No silent unit fallbacks
nodes.rationale: A missing or unknown unit must surface (raise or warn) rather than default, because a silent default is exactly the failure mode that turns a unit bug into a wrong scientific result nobody notices.

nodes.label: Tag-driven release trigger
nodes.rationale: Releases are cut only by pushing a v* tag, so the release artefact set is reproducible from a single immutable git ref rather than from a manual workflow_dispatch.

nodes.label: Version drift guard
nodes.rationale: The first step reads __version__ from _version.py and fails the build when it disagrees with the pushed tag, so a release binary can never advertise a version different from the tag that produced it. _version.py is the single source of truth; the guard is what enforces that claim in CI.

nodes.rationale: A loaded Quantity whose unit fell outside nM/uM/mM/M was silently reinterpreted with the combo box's stale unit; it is now converted to molar (or the file's unit is shown when selectable) with a notice.

nodes.label: Pint ~P/~H display formatting
nodes.rationale: Only the genuinely missing pieces are wrapped: negative-exponent reciprocals (1/M -> M^-1), domain math subscripts, and axis-tick scientific notation. A displayed unit is sourced from the value's own Quantity, not a registry re-lookup, so it stays correct for an assay absent from the registry; the a.u. alias is normalised first because Pint parses the dots as year*amu.

nodes.label: Initial Guess vs. Random Initialization
nodes.rationale: The first decision branches on whether a user-supplied initial guess exists: if so it seeds the parameter sets, otherwise starts are drawn randomly within bounds. Both branches converge on the same Generate Multiple Parameter Sets node, so a supplied guess biases the search without becoming the only start point.

nodes.label: Multi-start Trial Loop
nodes.rationale: The diagram loops Generate Parameter Sets -> Optimize -> Minimize Residuals -> Compute RMSE & R2 -> Filter -> More Trials? back onto itself. Repeating the local L-BFGS-B optimisation from many independent starting points is what keeps a non-convex binding-model fit from settling in a local minimum; a single deterministic start would be cheaper but would not survive a poorly conditioned Ka landscape. Quality metrics are computed per trial so the loop can discard bad basins instead of averaging them in.

nodes.label: Per-Replica Fitting Loop
nodes.rationale: The outer loop (More Replicas? -> back to Generate Multiple Parameter Sets) fits each experimental replica independently rather than fitting a pooled average, so replica-to-replica spread becomes a measurable uncertainty on the fitted constants. A replica whose trials all fail is skipped explicitly rather than silently dropped or back-filled.

nodes.label: F10: raw DimensionalityError on wrong x/y assay units
nodes.norm_label: f10: raw dimensionalityerror on wrong x/y assay units
nodes.rationale: A raw Pint DimensionalityError told the user nothing about the domain; the boundary now raises a ValueError naming what each axis must be (x = concentration, y = signal).

nodes.label: F8: self-describing TXT unit header
nodes.rationale: Raw TXT files were bare floats with no in-band unit, so the writer now emits a '# units:' header and the reader parses it — the file carries its own contract instead of relying on the M default.

nodes.label: Self-describing I/O unit contract
nodes.rationale: Readers declare a unit and every consumer must honor it — a declared unit is worthless if a consumer assumes M, which is exactly the three silent 1e6-1e9 errors the re-audit found. MeasurementSet.from_dataframe is the single normalization point.

nodes.label: No unit guessing from column names
nodes.norm_label: no unit guessing from column names
nodes.rationale: Heuristic label parsing (conc_M, [uM]) is itself a fragile classifier that could introduce the very silent errors this design removes, so declaration stays explicit — header, XUNITS, or the GUI selector — or the value is M by contract.

nodes.label: F9: read_raw_concentrations returned a bare array plus a unit string
nodes.norm_label: f9: read_raw_concentrations returned a bare array plus a unit string
nodes.rationale: Returning (ndarray, unit_str) let the magnitude and its unit drift apart at the call site; returning a Quantity keeps them inseparable.

nodes.label: H1: extract_concentrations_from_file ignored the declared unit
nodes.norm_label: h1: extract_concentrations_from_file ignored the declared unit
nodes.rationale: The reader declared the file's unit but this consumer wrapped face values as M, a silent 1e6-1e9 error; it now returns a self-describing Quantity in the declared unit.

nodes.label: H2: pd.concat dropped per-file unit attrs in batch import
nodes.norm_label: h2: pd.concat dropped per-file unit attrs in batch import
nodes.rationale: Concatenating replicate files discarded each frame's declared concentration unit, so a micromolar replicate stacked as molar; each file is now converted to molar via its own declared unit before the concat.

nodes.label: F3: silent micromolar fallback for an unknown x-axis unit
nodes.norm_label: f3: silent micromolar fallback for an unknown x-axis unit
nodes.rationale: A dict.get(x_unit, 1e6) default silently rescaled the plot when the unit was unrecognised; the replacement derives the scale through Pint and raises on an invalid unit.

nodes.label: F5: missing unit silently re-wrapped as dimensionless
nodes.norm_label: f5: missing unit silently re-wrapped as dimensionless
nodes.rationale: Importing a result or toggling median/mean re-attached a registry-looked-up unit and fell back to dimensionless, quietly loading a Ka as a bare number. from_dict now raises and the statistics toggle takes each unit from the fitted parameter itself.

nodes.label: F6: condition units dropped on export
nodes.norm_label: f6: condition units dropped on export

nodes.label: Magnitude + explicit unit token serialization
nodes.rationale: Because the app owns the registry, readable string tokens round-trip perfectly, so they are preferred over Pint's registry-independent to_tuple; parameters, conditions, x_fit/y_fit and custom_bounds all carry their own tokens, making the whole payload self-describing.

nodes.label: Convert with an explicit target, never to_base_units()
nodes.norm_label: convert with an explicit target, never to_base_units()
nodes.rationale: Molar's SI base is mol/m^3, so Q_(1,'M').to_base_units() yields 999.999... mol/m^3 — a 1000x error plus float noise. q.to('M').magnitude both converts and validates, raising DimensionalityError on a wrong-dimension input.

nodes.label: F1: _scale_factor classified units by .dimensionless
nodes.community_name: F2 (root cause): au defined as dimensionless and shadowing astronomical_unit
nodes.rationale: Classifying a unit component through the private unit._units mapping made au/M indistinguishable from 1/M; the fix classifies by the [signal] and [concentration] dimensions and leaves genuinely dimensionless components at factor 1.0.

nodes.label: F2 (root cause): au defined as dimensionless and shadowing astronomical_unit
nodes.community_name: F2 (root cause): au defined as dimensionless and shadowing astronomical_unit
nodes.norm_label: f2 (root cause): au defined as dimensionless and shadowing astronomical_unit
nodes.rationale: A dimensionless au made signal coefficients (au/M) dimensionally identical to binding constants (1/M) — the single highest scientific risk found. Redefining au = [signal] = a.u. removes the collision while keeping every serialization token and display string unchanged, so no data migration was needed.

nodes.label: au = [signal] custom dimension
nodes.community_name: F2 (root cause): au defined as dimensionless and shadowing astronomical_unit
nodes.rationale: Pint has no usable fluorescence unit and every dimensionless candidate keeps the collision, so au gets its own base dimension. That makes au/M distinct from 1/M, makes the 4-parameter signal law dimensionally checkable end to end, and keeps the 'au' token and 'a.u.' display symbol unchanged so no stored data migrates.

nodes.label: Validate units once per boundary crossing
nodes.community_name: F2 (root cause): au defined as dimensionless and shadowing astronomical_unit
nodes.norm_label: validate units once per boundary crossing

nodes.label: ParamKind plus [signal] dimension dual classification
nodes.community_name: F2 (root cause): au defined as dimensionless and shadowing astronomical_unit
nodes.rationale: Dimensional analysis alone cannot name a quantity, so identity is carried by two mutually reinforcing mechanisms: the [signal] dimension for unambiguous unit classification and ParamKind as the explicit label, cross-checked by a lint test so neither drifts.

nodes.label: Residual subtraction as a runtime signal-law check
nodes.community_name: F2 (root cause): au defined as dimensionless and shadowing astronomical_unit
nodes.norm_label: residual subtraction as a runtime signal-law check
nodes.rationale: forward_model must return an au Quantity; because residuals subtract it from y_data, a wrong-dimension model output raises at runtime without any decorator on the hot path.

nodes.label: Single shared UnitRegistry
nodes.community_name: F2 (root cause): au defined as dimensionless and shadowing astronomical_unit
nodes.rationale: Quantities from two registries raise on any mixed operation, so every module imports the one ureg/Q_ from core/units.py; set_application_registry makes it the process-wide default so pickled Quantities reconstruct against a registry that knows au and the molar prefixes.

nodes.label: Quantities at the edges, floats in the core
nodes.community_name: F2 (root cause): au defined as dimensionless and shadowing astronomical_unit
nodes.norm_label: quantities at the edges, floats in the core
nodes.rationale: Units are invariant across optimizer iterations, so re-checking them per call buys nothing: a bare-float forward model runs at 3.2 us/call, @ureg.wraps on the per-iteration model at 41 us (12.7x), while validating once at the boundary costs 1.01x. Speed is the reason, and the boundary validation is what makes it safe.
